items: initiative, strength, persistence, creative power

Strength that keeps moving brings things into being. Energy is plentiful now, and a clear aim can carry you far, as long as it stays true to what is right. Begin, keep going, and let steadiness rather than force be what sustains you.

Heaven above heaven: the sky turns without pause, day after day. Take it as your model: keep building your own strength, steadily and without letting up, rather than waiting for something outside to push you.
The dragon is still under the water. Your strength is real but not ready to show; keep preparing rather than acting now.
The dragon appears in the open field. Your abilities are starting to be seen; seek out people of experience who can help you grow.
Busy all day and still watchful in the evening. Effort brings you close to risk, but staying alert and honest keeps you from mistakes.
A leap that might rise or might fall back into the depths. You are free to go forward or to stay; choose from your own truth and there is no fault.
The dragon flies in the open sky. Your influence is at its best; use it generously and keep wise counsel near.
The dragon that climbs too high. Pushing past the natural limit leads to regret; know when enough is enough.
receptivity, support, patience, nurturing

The earth receives, carries and brings to fruit whatever is given to it. This is a time to follow rather than lead, to support a good aim and let it grow through you. Steady, gentle devotion, like a mare that keeps walking across open country, achieves more now than pushing ahead alone. Companions found along the way matter.
Earth upon earth: the ground stretches wide and holds everything without complaint. Let your character be broad and generous enough to carry what is entrusted to you.
Frost underfoot on an autumn morning means ice is on its way. Notice small early signs and respond while it is still easy.
Straight, square and wide, like open land. Act from your plain, natural goodness; nothing needs to be forced or rehearsed.
Keep your gifts quietly in reserve. If you serve a larger task, help bring it to completion without needing the credit.
A sack tied shut. Holding back and staying discreet earns neither praise nor blame, and that is fine for now.
A plain yellow garment, worn without show. Real worth expressed modestly brings great good fortune.
Dragons clash in the open field and both are wounded. Holding your ground long past the point of yielding leads to a fight nobody wins.
new beginnings, growing pains, perseverance, asking for help

Something new is pressing upward through confusion, like a sprout pushing through hard ground. Things feel tangled, but this is the mess of growth, not failure. Don't rush toward distant goals; keep going steadily, and find helpers who can bring order to the chaos.
Thunder rumbles beneath heavy rain clouds: a storm is gathering before the rain breaks. In times like this, sort out the tangle thread by thread and put things in order.
An obstacle at the very start makes you hesitate. Don't push through blindly; hold to your aim and gather people who can help.
Difficulties pile up, and an offer arrives that isn't quite right. Wait patiently for what truly fits, even if it takes a long time.
Chasing the deer into the forest without a guide only gets you lost. Recognize when to stop rather than pressing on alone.
You can't manage this alone, and help is offered. Accept the connection and move forward together; it goes well.
You have good things to give, but they are hard to share right now. Small, careful steps work; a grand push would backfire.
Stuck and in tears, with the horses pulling apart. Don't stay in this despair; the sorrow eases once you look for another way.
learning, inexperience, humility, guidance

Not knowing is where all learning starts. Things go well when the student seeks out the teacher, not the other way round, and when a question is asked sincerely. Asking the same question again and again out of impatience only muddies the answer. Stay open, be patient, and keep at it.
Water springs out at the base of a mountain, fresh and not yet sure where it will flow. Be thorough in what you do, and let your character grow the way a spring fills each hollow before it moves on.
A little discipline at the start helps a learner focus. Use structure to free them, not to punish; too much strictness backfires.
Be patient and kind with those who don't yet know. Bearing with others' mistakes generously shows you are ready for responsibility.
Don't lose yourself chasing someone who seems impressive. Giving up your own ground to please another leads nowhere good.
Caught up in daydreams that don't touch reality. Clinging to fantasy brings embarrassment; come back to what is real.
Approach the matter like a child: open, curious and willing to be taught. This simple humility brings good fortune.
When correcting a mistake, aim only to stop the harm. Firmness helps; anger and punishment for their own sake do not.
patience, timing, confidence, nourishment

What you want lies on the far side of a delay or a danger, and the moment to cross has not yet come. Waiting is not empty when you trust the outcome and stay honest with yourself about where you stand. Keep your strength up, eat and rest well, and when the time is right you can cross the great water.
Clouds have climbed into the sky: rain is coming, but not yet. Meanwhile eat, drink and be at ease, keeping your spirits steady while the weather ripens.
Waiting out in the open meadow, far from trouble. Keep up your ordinary routine and don't waste energy worrying.
Waiting on the sand near the water. Some talk or criticism comes your way; stay calm and it ends well.
Waiting in the mud at the water's edge. Having moved too soon, you've left yourself exposed; be careful now.
Waiting in the thick of danger. Stay steady, don't thrash about, and you can find your way out of the pit.
Waiting over food and wine. Even in the middle of a hard stretch, take this calm moment to rest and enjoy; steadiness brings good fortune.
Fallen into the pit, then three unexpected visitors arrive. Welcome them with respect, even if they weren't what you hoped for; they may be the way out.
dispute, compromise, caution, fairness

You feel you are in the right, yet you are blocked. Staying wary and stopping halfway, open to a fair settlement, brings good results; pushing the dispute to the bitter end does not. Look for a fair-minded person who can see the matter clearly, and don't launch any big undertaking while the conflict lasts.

The sky pulls upward while water runs downward, each moving away from the other. Before you begin anything, think carefully about how it starts, so that conflict doesn't grow from the very first step.
Let the quarrel drop while it is still small. A few words may be said, but things end well.
You can't win this fight against a stronger side. Stepping back and going home protects you and the people around you.
Rely on what you have honestly earned instead of grasping for more. Quietly keeping to it brings things right in the end, though not without strain.
You could fight, but you choose not to. Turning back and changing your stance brings a peace that lasts.
Bring the matter before someone wise and fair. An honest judgment settles it, and that brings great good fortune.
A prize won by fighting to the end is soon taken away again. Victory through conflict does not stay with you.
discipline, leadership, organization, shared purpose

A group needs direction to get anything done, and that direction must come from someone experienced and trusted. Discipline is necessary, but it holds only when people believe in the aim and in the one who leads. With a just cause and a steady leader, the effort succeeds without harm.
Water held within the earth, like ground water quietly feeding the land. Be generous and patient with people, and their strength gathers around you.
Set out in good order or not at all. A plan that starts in confusion goes badly.
The leader stays among the people and shares their work. This earns trust and recognition, and things go well.
Too many people giving orders, and the effort falters. Muddled leadership brings loss.
The group pulls back. A wise retreat in the face of superior odds is no mistake.
There is real trouble in the field, and it must be dealt with. Let the most experienced person lead; putting the wrong person in charge brings misfortune, however determined they are.
The work is done and rewards are handed out. Be fair, but don't give real power to those who can't carry it.
union, loyalty, belonging, trust

People draw together around a center they can trust. If you are that center, ask yourself honestly whether you are worthy of it; if you are thinking of joining, don't hesitate too long. Those who arrive late may find the circle already closed.
Water lying on the earth, running together into pools wherever the ground allows. Build close ties with others the way water gathers on the land.
Sincerity is the start of any bond. Be genuine, like a plain bowl filled to the brim, and good things come to you from beyond.
Hold to the bond from the inside, out of real feeling and not to win favor. Staying true to yourself brings good fortune.
You may be close to the wrong people. Be friendly, but don't give your deepest trust where it doesn't belong.
Show your loyalty openly to someone worth following. Steadiness in this brings good fortune.
The best union is freely chosen. Leave the gate open: let those who want to come stay, and let those who want to go leave.
The moment for joining has passed without a commitment. Without a center to hold to, things go badly.
gentle restraint, patience, small steps, influence

Heavy clouds gather in the west, but the rain has not come. Your strength is held back for now by something small and soft, and forcing it won't help. Work gently and kindly, take care of the details, and trust that what is held back is building toward its time.
Wind moving high across the sky, gathering clouds that do not yet rain. Refine the smaller, outward things in yourself while the larger moment approaches.
Held back, you return to your own path. That is no fault, and it brings good fortune.
Seeing others turn back, you are drawn to return as well. Following that sensible example is wise.
Pushing ahead anyway, the wheel's spokes break and tempers flare at home. Forcing what is blocked leads to quarrels.
Honest intentions dissolve fear and danger. Sincerity lets a gentle person restrain a strong one without harm.
Bonds of trust mean your neighbors' riches are shared with you, and yours with them. Shared good faith multiplies what each of you has.
The rain has come and things settle. Like a moon that is nearly full, you have reached enough; pressing further now brings misfortune.
conduct, courtesy, care, respect

You step on the tiger's tail and it does not bite. Even in a delicate or risky situation, good manners, a light touch and respect can carry you safely past someone stronger. Know where you stand, act with grace, and the danger stays calm.
The sky overhead and the lake beneath, each at its proper level. Learn to tell high from low, and let that clarity settle people's minds and steady what they aim for.
Walk simply and honestly. Plain conduct without ambition lets you move ahead without fault.
A quiet person walks a smooth, level road. Staying modest and keeping out of entanglements brings good fortune.
Overrating your own sight and strength, you step on the tiger's tail and it bites. Know your limits before taking a risk.
You step on the tiger's tail, but with great care. Caution and respect see you through to a good end.
Walking with firm resolve, knowing the danger. Determination is needed here, but stay aware of the risks it carries.
Look back at the road you have walked and see what it led to. If your conduct holds up, great good fortune follows.
harmony, prosperity, flow, balance

What is petty is leaving and what is great is on its way. Heaven and earth meet, and everything that grows between them thrives. This is a time of ease and good connection; enjoy it, share what it brings, and use it to strengthen what will carry you through the next change.
Earth above and heaven below, meeting and mingling so that life can flourish. Shape and support this flow wisely, helping things find their natural course.
Pull up one blade of grass and the roots of others come with it. Like-minded people move together, and setting out now goes well.
Be gentle with the rough, bold when crossing the river, mindful of what is far away, and free of favoritism. That is how to walk the middle way.
Level ground always tilts somewhere, and whatever leaves eventually returns. Stay steady when things turn, and enjoy the good you still have.
Those with plenty come down to meet their neighbors without show. Simple, sincere trust holds them together.
Someone of high standing joins with a humbler one in true partnership. Setting pride aside brings blessing and great good fortune.
The wall slides back into the moat. The good time is turning; don't fight it with force, but tend to those closest to you.
stagnation, withdrawal, integrity, waiting it out

Heaven and earth have drawn apart, and nothing flows between them. What is great is leaving and what is petty draws near. In a time like this, influence tends to go to the wrong places; keep your integrity, don't trade your values for a seat at the table, and conserve your strength until things shift.

The sky rises away and the earth sinks below, and nothing passes between them. Keep your gifts quiet and live simply, turn down rewards that would compromise you, and stay out of the scramble for position.
Pull up one blade of grass and others come with it. When the times are wrong, step back together with those who share your values.
Others try to win you over with flattery and easy favors, and those who go along may do well for a while. Your own way through is to keep apart from it.
Those who rose by wrong means begin to feel ashamed. That stirring of conscience is the first small change.
A turning point arrives, and you act from a sense of something higher than yourself. There is no blame, and those with you share in the good.
The standstill is beginning to lift, and good fortune comes. Keep a healthy doubt in mind and fasten your hopes to something firm, like a rope tied to deep-rooted mulberry.
The standstill ends. First the stuck time, then good fortune, though it takes your own effort to bring the change about.
fellowship, community, openness, shared goals

Fellowship that happens in the open, where everyone can see. When people come together around something larger than private interests, even great difficulties can be crossed. Keep the circle open rather than forming cliques, and let clear shared values, not personal favor, be what holds it together.
Fire rising toward heaven, flame and sky reaching the same way. Bring order to a group by recognizing the different kinds of people within it and giving each their place.
Meeting others at the gate, out in the open. Starting a connection with no hidden agenda is free of fault.
Keeping fellowship only within your own clan. Favoring insiders narrows the circle and brings regret.
Hiding weapons in the bushes and watching from the hill. Mistrust keeps you on guard for years and gets you nowhere.
Up on the wall, ready to attack, you stop. Seeing that fighting is wrong, you turn back, and that brings good fortune.
Those who belong together are kept apart, and at first they weep. After a hard struggle they meet, and then they laugh.
Fellowship out in the far meadow. The bond is loose and not yet the deepest kind, but there is nothing to regret.
abundance, generosity, clarity, responsibility

A time of great possession, and it goes very well. Strength within and clarity without bring plenty, whether in resources, ability or goodwill. Wealth of any kind is held well when it is shared, kept modest and put to good use.
The sun blazes high in the sky, shining on everything below. Bring the good into the light and let the bad fall away, staying in tune with what is right.
Plenty has not yet tempted you into harm. Stay aware of the difficulties that wealth brings and you remain without fault.
A big wagon, ready to be loaded. You have the means and the helpers to carry something worthwhile; go ahead.
Offer what you have to something greater than yourself. A small-minded person would keep it, but generosity is the point.
Don't try to outshine those around you. Keeping your distance from rivalry and display keeps you free of blame.
Be open and sincere with others while keeping your dignity. Trust given freely, with quiet authority, brings good fortune.
Blessed from above. When abundance is held with humility and respect, everything works out well.
humility, balance, fairness, quiet success

Modesty opens the way. The one who doesn't make much of themselves can carry things through to the end. Just as water fills hollows and wears down peaks, life tends to even out what is too high and too low; staying modest puts you on the side of that balance.
A mountain hidden within the earth: great height that does not stand out. Take from what is overfull and add to what is lacking, weighing things so that each gets its fair share.
So modest you don't even make a point of being modest. With nothing to prove, you can take on even a great crossing, and it goes well.
Modesty that shows naturally in how you speak and act. Staying true to it brings good fortune.
Real merit, held modestly. Working hard without seeking credit, you see things through to a good end.
Modesty that shows in action. Don't use humility as an excuse to hold back; do your part fully and openly.
No boasting in front of your neighbors. Still, when something must be done firmly, act; modesty doesn't mean weakness.
Modesty that has become well known. Turn its strength inward and put your own house in order before anyone else's.
enthusiasm, inspiration, readiness, momentum

Enthusiasm moves people. When the one in front is in tune with the mood of the moment, others follow willingly, and it becomes possible to set helpers in place and get things moving. Prepare in good time, and let the energy run along natural lines rather than forcing it.
Thunder bursts out of the earth and the land comes alive. Music and shared celebration bring people together and connect them with what matters most.
Boasting out loud about your excitement or your connections. Showing it off this way brings misfortune.
Steady as stone, you aren't carried away by the mood around you. Seeing early when to step back, you don't need a whole day to decide, and that brings good fortune.
Waiting for someone above to give you enthusiasm, or hesitating too long. Either way leads to regret; find your own pace.
You are the source of the enthusiasm, and great things come of it. Trust yourself, and others gather around you like hair held by a single pin.
A constant pressure that never quite lets up keeps you from being swept away by pleasure. It is wearing, but it also keeps you alert.
Carried away by enthusiasm that no longer fits. Even after the fact, a change of heart frees you from blame.
adapting, trust, joining, rest

Following goes well when it is freely chosen. To be followed, first learn to follow: adapt to what the moment asks, and people will trust you because you are trustworthy. Stay true to what is right, and joining in brings no regret.
Thunder rests inside the lake, like the year's energy settling down for winter. When the day grows dark, go home and rest; moving with the rhythm of the time is a strength, not a defeat.
What you have been holding to is shifting. Step outside your usual circle and listen to people who think differently; a fair mind finds good company there.
Clinging to what is small and easy can cost you what is worthwhile. Choose your company with care, because you cannot follow both.
Letting go of a lesser attachment frees you to follow something truly worthwhile. You lose some comfort and gain direction; stay steady in that choice.

People begin to follow you, some only for what they can gain, and holding on to such a following brings trouble. Check your own motives and keep your purpose honest; that clarity keeps you free of blame.
Your faith in what is good is sincere. Following what you truly value brings good fortune now.
Someone who had stepped away is held fast by those who need them, and comes back. A bond this deep is honored, and your experience is asked for again.
repair, inheritance, renewal, responsibility

Something has spoiled through neglect, and it can be put right. Don't only tidy the surface: look carefully at how the decay began before you act, and keep watching afterwards so it does not slip back. Work done this way is worth the effort, even when it is a big undertaking.
Wind blows low along the foot of the mountain, stirring what has gone still. Shake up what has grown stale in yourself and those around you, then strengthen it patiently.
A habit or rule handed down to you has gone wrong. Fixing it is no betrayal of those who came before; there is some risk, but care brings a good end.
What was spoiled through softness or neglect needs mending, but gently. Being too harsh about old weakness only wounds; correct it with tact.
You go at an old problem a little too forcefully. Some regret follows, yet acting too strongly is far better than doing nothing.
You let an old fault stand because facing it feels hard. Putting it off only lets the rot spread, and it ends in embarrassment.
You take on an old mess and set it right, with help from others. The work earns real respect.
You step back from public affairs to tend something higher in yourself. This is not indifference; inner work can matter just as much.
approach, growth, warmth, timing

Something good is drawing near, and strength is rising like days lengthening after winter. Meet it with warmth and steady effort while the season favors you. Every rising season turns again, so use this one well instead of assuming it will last.
The earth stands above the lake, a shore that both overlooks the water and holds it. Teach, care for and make room for others with a patience that does not run out.
You approach together with others who share your aim. Keep to what is right and things go well.
Moving forward side by side with others, you meet with success. Don't worry yet about the season turning; everything works now.
An easy, comfortable approach, all sweet words and little behind them, gets you nowhere. Once you notice this and regret it, the mistake fades.
You meet people openly and fully, holding nothing back. There is no blame in that.
Wise leadership draws in capable people and lets them do their work. Knowing what to hand over is a wisdom of its own.
You come back generously to help others, with nothing to gain for yourself. Large-hearted kindness like this brings good fortune.
observation, perspective, example, reflection

Step back and look before you act. Like someone who has washed their hands for a ceremony but not yet made the offering, stay in that moment of gathered, quiet attention. When you are sincere, others feel it without being told.
Wind moves across the earth, touching everything it passes. Go out and look closely at how people actually live, and let what you see shape how you guide them.
You look at things the way a child does, without the bigger picture. That is fine for someone with little responsibility, but not for anyone who must lead.
You see the world through the crack of a door and take your small view for the whole. It may do for a narrow life, but a wider view is needed now.
Look at your own life and what it brings about. Your own effects, not other people's opinions, tell you whether to go forward or step back.
You see clearly how a place or group truly flourishes. Offer your gifts there as a respected guest rather than trying to take charge.
Others look to you, so look honestly at your own life. If what you bring about is good, you are free of blame.
Look at your life from a little distance, as if it belonged to someone else. Free of ego, you see what matters and are without blame.
decision, obstacle, fairness, clarity

Something stands in the way, like a piece of gristle that keeps the jaws from closing. Bite through it: name the obstacle plainly and deal with it firmly and fairly. Clear, measured consequences let things flow again.
Thunder and lightning arrive together, force and clarity at once. Make your boundaries plain and your consequences fair, so no one has to guess.
A first small misstep is caught early, like feet held briefly in the stocks. A light correction now spares a heavier one later; no blame.
You bite so hard into something soft that you go too far. The reaction is a bit much, but the cause was real; no blame.
You bite into something old and tough and hit something sour. Your standing is questioned and it stings a little, yet the job still needed doing.
The obstacle is hard and the resistance strong. Stay straight as an arrow and solid as metal, mindful of the difficulty, and persistence brings good fortune.
The matter is hard to settle, but your fairness is golden. Stay aware of the risk and keep to the middle way; no blame.
Someone has stopped listening altogether, as if a heavy collar covered their ears. Ignoring every warning leads to misfortune; open your ears while you still can.
beauty, form, simplicity, style

Grace and beauty help small matters go smoothly. Style, manners and good presentation are real gifts, but they adorn what is already there and cannot replace it. Enjoy the beauty, and don't make big decisions on looks alone.
A fire burns at the foot of the mountain, lighting its slopes beautifully but only a little way up. Use that light to bring order to everyday things, but don't settle serious disputes by appearances.
You make your feet graceful by leaving the comfortable carriage and walking. Choose the honest, simpler path over borrowed ease.
Grace like a beard on a chin: it follows the face it grows on. Attend to what lies underneath before what decorates it.
Everything feels graceful and glowing, almost too easy. Enjoy it, but stay steady and don't let comfort dull you.
You wonder whether to choose polish or plain simplicity. Someone sincere arrives quickly, as if on a white horse, not as a threat but as a friend; choose what is genuine.
You seek out a quiet, simple place and the people who matter, though your gift seems small. It may feel awkward, but sincerity outweighs show, and it ends well.
Plain, unadorned grace. When form and substance finally agree, nothing more is needed; no blame.
decline, letting go, patience, endings
Things are coming apart, slowly, from underneath. This is not the moment to push forward or start something new. Accept the season, keep quiet, and protect what matters most; it will pass.
The mountain rests on the earth, and only a broad base keeps it standing. Make your footing secure by being generous to the people and the ground that hold you up.
The legs of the bed are being worn away; the trouble starts at the very bottom. Holding stubbornly to your position only hurts you now, so wait.
The frame of the bed splits as well. You are alone and the trouble is close; stay careful and flexible rather than rigid.
You break with those who are undermining what is good, even if it leaves you lonely. Siding with what is right is no mistake.
The damage reaches your own skin. The decline is personal now; accept it rather than fighting blindly, for force will not stop it.
Like a line of fish swimming in order, scattered parts fall into place behind a good leader. The tide turns, and everything works out.
One large fruit is still uneaten, a seed of what comes next. What is good finds new ground to stand on, while those who tore things down lose their own shelter.
return, turning point, renewal, rest

After the darkest point, the light comes back. A turning has arrived by itself; don't hurry it. Let things return in their own time, welcome friends who come back, and move gently in the new direction.
Thunder sleeps inside the earth: new life is stirring underground. At the turn of the year, people of old rested and kept quiet so the fresh energy could grow without being spent.
You turn back after only a short way off course. There is nothing to regret; great good fortune.
You return quietly, encouraged by good people nearby. Coming back with grace brings good fortune.
You keep returning and then straying again. It is unsettled, yet each return is better than staying lost; no blame.
You walk with a crowd but turn back alone toward what you know is right. It may be lonely, and it is the true way.
You return with an open heart and own your mistakes. No regret.
You miss the moment to turn back and press on stubbornly. Trouble comes from inside and out; take a long pause before trying again.
sincerity, naturalness, spontaneity, trust

Act from a clear, natural heart, without hidden plans. What you do sincerely and in step with the moment tends to go well. But innocence is not carelessness: if your motives are off, even good luck turns sour, so check them first.
Thunder rolls beneath the open sky and every living thing wakes as it should. In the same way, give each person and each task what it truly needs, in its own season.
Acting from a pure, unforced impulse brings good fortune. Trust your first honest instinct.
Plow without counting the harvest; clear the field without already spending what it will yield. Do the work for its own sake, and you can go ahead.
Something goes wrong that you did not cause, like a passer-by leading off a cow tied up in your village. Luck is sometimes unfair; don't let it make you bitter.
Stay with what is truly yours. If you keep steady on your own ground, you cannot go wrong.
A trouble that was not of your making often clears up on its own. Don't reach for drastic fixes that create new problems; give it time.
Even innocent action is out of season now. Wait quietly instead of pushing; nothing would come of acting.
restraint, stored strength, learning, readiness

Great energy is being held and gathered rather than wasted. Keep steady, learn from what came before, and put your strength to work beyond your own four walls. This is a good time to take on something big.
Heaven held inside the mountain: a vast treasure kept in stillness. Fill yourself with what the wise said and did before you, and let it deepen your character.
Danger lies ahead, and something holds you back. Stop for now; stopping is not losing.
The block that holds the cart to its axle has been taken out, so the cart stays where it stands. Accept the delay calmly; holding back is the wise choice.
The way opens and you race ahead like a good horse among others. Stay alert to danger and practice your skills every day; then it is good to have somewhere to go.
A board is fixed across a young bull's horns before they grow. Restraining wildness early, before it does harm, brings great good fortune.
A boar's tusks are dangerous, but its wildness can be tamed at the root. Address the source of a problem rather than fighting its symptoms; good fortune.
The blockage gives way and the road to the sky opens. What has been stored up can now be used freely; success.
nourishment, care, words, self-reliance

Notice what nourishes you and what you feed others. You learn a lot about someone from what they care for and what they reach for. Pay attention both to what you take in and to the words you send out.
Thunder stirs at the foot of the still mountain, like a jaw moving beneath a firm skull. Be careful with what you say and moderate in what you take in.
You set aside your own steady source of nourishment and stare at someone else's plate. Envy drains you; come back to what you already have.
You look for support from those above you or far off your path instead of standing on your own feet. Going on this way leads to trouble.
You reach for things that satisfy for a moment but never truly nourish. Stay away from that path; nothing good comes of it.
You look upward for help so that you can look after others, keen and watchful as a tiger. Seeking support for a good cause is right; no blame.
You know you cannot do this alone, so you lean on someone wiser. Stay steady with that support, and don't attempt a great crossing yet.
You have become a source of nourishment for others. Hold that responsibility with care, and even great undertakings are open to you.
pressure, overload, decisive action, courage

Too much weight rests on too little support, and the main roof beam is bending. This cannot hold for long, so act: find a way out or a way to share the load. Move with gentle firmness rather than panic, and things can still go well.
The lake rises over the treetops, an unusual flood. In such a time, stand alone without fear if you must, and step back from the world without losing heart.
You lay down soft white mats before setting the heavy load on the ground. Great care at the start is not too much now; no blame.
An old tree sends up fresh shoots from its root. An unexpected partnership renews you, and everything goes well.
The beam bends further and finally cracks. Pushing on alone and refusing help leads to misfortune.
The beam is braced and holds. Good fortune, as long as you use the support honestly and not for your own gain.
An old tree puts out flowers, but its roots are not renewed. A showy late bloom without depth: nothing wrong, and nothing to praise either.
You wade in to finish what must be done and find yourself in over your head. Things go badly and the cost is high, yet acting for what you believe in is no fault.
danger, faith, persistence, flow

Difficulty follows difficulty, like water falling into one hollow after another. Don't freeze and don't panic. Hold on to what you know is true in your heart; that inner steadiness carries you through and gives your actions weight.
Water flows on and on, filling each hollow before moving ahead, until it reaches the sea. Be steady and consistent in good conduct, and pass on what you know by patient repetition.
You have grown used to danger and slipped deeper into it without noticing. Getting comfortable with what is wrong leads to misfortune.
The hollow is dangerous and you cannot climb out all at once. Aim for small, reachable steps; that is enough for now.
Every way forward or back seems to lead into another pit. Stop and wait instead of struggling; any move now makes things worse.
A modest gift of wine and rice in plain earthenware is handed over through a window, not with ceremony at the door. In hard times simple sincerity is enough; no blame.
The pit is not overflowing; the water has risen just level with its edge and will soon find its way out. Don't try to do everything at once; leave by the easiest route, and there is no blame.
Tied up and caught in a thicket of thorns, you cannot find a way out for a long while. Having lost your bearings, expect a hard stretch and allow the time it takes to find them again.
clarity, light, dependence, attention

Fire has no shape of its own; it shines only by clinging to what it burns. Know what you depend on and choose it well. Steadiness and a gentle, caring attitude, like tending a patient cow, keep your light bright.
Fire above fire: one light follows another, as the sun comes up again each morning. Keep your own light steady and let it reach every corner around you.
Morning begins and footsteps cross in every direction. Pause and collect yourself before rushing in; serious attention keeps you clear of mistakes.
A warm golden light, like the sun at noon. Balance and moderation bring great good fortune.
As the sun goes down, some bang on a pot and sing while others mourn their advancing years. Both miss the point; accept that everything passes, without forced cheer or despair.
It flares up all at once, burns out and is cast aside. A blaze that rises too fast does not last; find a steadier fuel.
Tears flow and there is sighing. A real change of heart, deeply felt, brings good fortune.
Clear up a deep disorder by dealing with its source, not by punishing everyone involved. Be firm and fair, without harshness; no blame.
attraction, openness, courtship, mutuality

Two forces draw each other in and are moved by each other. Real influence works through openness and gentleness, not pressure. Stay sincere and receptive, and a bond formed this way is a good one, in love as elsewhere.
A lake rests on top of a mountain: the mountain holds the water and the water nourishes the mountain. Keep a space open in yourself so others feel welcome to come near.
The stirring is felt in your big toe; a wish is there but not yet visible to anyone. Notice it without acting on it yet.
The urge to move reaches your calves. Running ahead now would be a mistake; waiting brings good fortune.
The pull reaches your thighs, and you chase whatever moves you or whoever tugs you along. Acting on every impulse leads to regret.
Now the heart is moved. Steady sincerity wins out; if you scheme and fret, you reach only the few people you are deliberately trying to win.
The influence settles in the back of your neck, firm and unmoved. You won't be swayed and won't go wrong, though you won't move others much either.
This time the stirring goes no further than the mouth. Talk alone, however clever, changes very little.
endurance, consistency, commitment, steadiness

What lasts is not what stands still, but what keeps moving in a steady, renewing rhythm. Stay true to your direction while letting your methods change with the times. Consistency like this brings success and leaves nothing to regret.
Thunder and wind always travel together, restless yet constant companions. Stand firm in yourself and don't keep changing course.
You want something permanent too quickly and ask too much at once. Lasting things grow slowly; forcing them goes nowhere.
You have more strength than the situation needs, but you keep it in check. Regret disappears.
Your mood shifts with every passing feeling, so others cannot rely on you. Inconsistency like this keeps bringing embarrassment.
You keep hunting in a field where there is no game. Persistence in the wrong place yields nothing; look somewhere else.
Steady loyalty to what is serves well when your role is to support. When you must lead, faithfulness also needs fresh judgment about what has changed.
Restlessness that never settles, always stirring, becomes its own trap. It leads to misfortune.
withdrawal, timing, dignity, distance

Some forces are rising that you can't stop by pushing against them, and the wise move is to step back while you can still choose how. Retreat here is not defeat; it keeps your strength whole for a better moment. Small, steady acts of integrity still go well, even while you give ground on the larger field.
Mountain below Heaven: however high the peak climbs, the sky keeps its distance. Hold yourself a little apart from what drains you, calmly and courteously, without anger and without slamming doors.
You are at the tail of the retreat, closest to the trouble. This is no time to start anything; staying quiet and still is the safer course.
You are held as firmly as if bound with a strap of yellow oxhide. A loyalty or purpose you are sure of keeps you in place, and that steadiness deserves respect.
A retreat that keeps getting halted by ties and obligations is uncomfortable and a little risky. Look after the people who depend on you in small ways, but don't let them steer the larger decision.
You step away by your own free choice. For someone at peace with the decision it is a clean move; it only stings if you were holding on for appearances.
A friendly, well-timed retreat: you leave on good terms and at the right moment. Holding steady to that choice serves you well.
A cheerful retreat, free of doubt and second thoughts. With nothing left to cling to, every road is open.
strength, momentum, restraint, principle

Your strength is real and growing, and the temptation is to use all of it at once. Power stays great only when it is joined to what is fair and right. Move with your force, but let principle, not appetite, decide where it goes.
Thunder above Heaven: a great roar rolling across the sky. Real strength shows in refusing to take paths that aren't yours to take.
All the power is in your toes, eager to march before the ground is ready. Pushing ahead from such a shaky footing tends to go badly; wait until your stance is sound.
Steadiness pays off here. You have strength in reserve, so keep to the middle way and don't overreach.
A ram charges a hedge and gets its horns tangled. Those who flaunt their power get stuck; the wiser person knows they could charge and quietly chooses not to.
The hedge opens and nothing snags. Quiet, steady force works like the axle of a heavy cart: unseen, it carries the whole load forward.
Let the stubborn goat go without a fight. Dropping a hard-headed stance costs you nothing worth keeping.
The ram is stuck in the hedge and can go neither forward nor back. Admit the difficulty plainly; seeing it clearly is what eventually frees you.
advance, recognition, clarity, sunrise

Like the sun climbing over the land, things are moving up and into the light. A generous, capable person gets noticed and welcomed, again and again within a single day. Progress of this kind rests on serving something larger than yourself and letting your good qualities be seen.
Fire above Earth: the sun rising over the land. Let your own light come out, polishing what is bright in you instead of waiting for others to do it.
You set out and are turned back, or met with doubt. Stay calm and good-natured; quiet persistence without resentment keeps your path clear.
Progress comes, but with worry or sadness attached. Keep going steadily; support may come from an older, caring figure who sees your worth.
The people around you agree and lend their support. With that trust behind you, old regrets fall away.
Advancing like a hamster that hoards whatever it grabs. Gains taken greedily or in secret are shaky, and climbing this way invites trouble.
Regret falls away. Don't fixate on what you win or lose; act in good faith and things tend to go well.
Charging ahead with lowered horns is fitting only for setting your own house in order, not for pushing others around. Aggression here carries risk, and clinging to it leaves you embarrassed.
adversity, inner light, discretion, endurance

The light has gone down into the earth, and the times don't reward openness. Keep your inner light burning, but shield it, and let your outward manner be modest and quiet. Holding to what is true in you through a hard stretch is what carries you to the other side.
Fire beneath Earth: the sun has sunk below the ground. Move among others without drawing attention, veiling your brightness while still seeing clearly.
You fly with drooping wings, leaving a place that is turning dark, even if it means going without comforts for a while. People may talk; let them, and keep moving.
You are wounded, but in the left thigh, not the heart. Use whatever strength you have, like a strong horse, to carry yourself and others out.
While hunting in the south, you catch the chief source of the darkness. Don't expect everything to set right at once; old habits take time to change.
You get close to the heart of the darkness and understand it from the inside. That knowledge lets you leave the gate and courtyard behind while there is still time.
Like Prince Ji, who hid his insight to survive a cruel court, you keep your light hidden while staying true. Quiet steadiness is the right stance.
No brightness left, only gloom: what climbed up to the sky has fallen into the depths. Darkness that overreaches undoes itself.
home, roles, care, trust

Order and warmth begin at home, in the closest circle of people you share daily life with. When each person knows their part and keeps their word, the whole household holds steady. The quiet, faithful care of whoever tends the inner life of the home is what makes it work.
Wind rising from Fire: the warmth of the hearth sends its influence outward. Say things that mean something and keep your habits steady, so what you say at home matches how you live.
Set clear, kind limits within the family early, before habits harden. Doing it now spares regret later.
Rather than chasing your own whims, attend to the everyday nourishment of the household. That steady attention is the heart of things here.
If the household runs hot and you come down too hard, you may regret it, yet that does less harm than letting everything slide into giggling chaos. Find the balance between firmness and ease.
Someone who keeps the household well provided for and well tended enriches everyone in it. Quiet stewardship brings real good.
Lead the family the way a good ruler would, through love rather than fear. When trust runs both ways, there is nothing to dread.
Your conduct earns respect because it is sincere. Over the long run, a person of real character gives the whole home its footing.
difference, estrangement, small steps, perspective

Two forces pull in different directions, like fire rising and water sinking. Large joint undertakings are hard right now, but small matters can still go well. Differences are not only a problem: they can show each side more clearly what it is.
Fire above Lake: the flames rise while the water settles lower. Among others, stay yourself; you can join in fully without giving up who you are.
If your horse runs off, don't chase it; it tends to find its own way back. Meet difficult people politely so you don't make a needless enemy.
You run into someone important in a narrow lane rather than at the formal gate. An informal meeting can bridge a gap that official channels can't.
The cart is dragged back, the oxen are halted, and you feel thwarted and even shamed. A rough start like this can still lead to a good ending.
Isolated by disagreement, you meet someone who sees things as you do. Trust each other in good faith and the danger passes.
Regret falls away. Someone close bites through what kept you apart as easily as through soft skin, and going to meet them is no mistake.

Lonely and suspicious, you see a friend as a pig caked in mud or a cart full of demons, and you draw your bow. Then you lower it, because this is a friend and not a foe; as the tension breaks like rain, things can turn out well.
obstacle, reflection, allies, patience

The way ahead is blocked, like a steep mountain with a torrent beyond it. Pressing straight into the obstacle helps no one; turning toward easier ground, seeking good counsel and working with others does. Use the halt to look inward and strengthen yourself.
Water on top of the Mountain: a torrent bars the way up. When you meet a barrier, look first at yourself and work on who you are.
Going forward runs into obstacles, while holding back earns respect. Wait for the right moment.
Obstacle piles on obstacle, but it isn't your fault; you are facing them out of duty to others. Keep going without blaming yourself.
Going on leads into trouble, so you turn back to those who need you. Your return is welcome.
Going alone leads to obstruction, while coming back to join others brings the strength you need. Gather allies before you try again.
Just when the way is most blocked, friends show up. Steadiness at the center draws helpers to you.
Pressing on leads to obstruction, while coming back to help others leads to great good. Seek out someone wise and experienced, and let them guide the next step.
release, relief, forgiveness, fresh start

A storm breaks and the air clears; what was knotted begins to loosen. Return to ordinary life as soon as you can, and if loose ends remain, tidy them quickly. Don't drag out the aftermath; let relief be relief.
Thunder above Water: thunder and rain burst out and clear the sky. Forgive what went wrong and let small offenses go, so the release can be complete.
The tension is gone. Rest a moment and recover; there is nothing here to fix.
In the field you catch three sly foxes and earn a yellow arrow, a sign of straight, honest action. Clearing out deceit with integrity is the right course.
Someone carrying a load on their back yet riding in a fine carriage invites robbers. Putting on airs you haven't earned draws the wrong attention, so keep it simple.
Free yourself from the hangers-on clinging to your big toe. Once you do, a true companion can come near, and trust between you can grow.
Only you can release yourself from what holds you. When you clearly do, even those who doubted you take you seriously.
The prince shoots a hawk perched on a high wall and brings it down. One clean, well-aimed act at the right moment removes the last obstacle.
simplicity, sincerity, letting go, restraint

Something has to be reduced, and when it is done sincerely, less can be enough. A simple offering given honestly means more than an elaborate one given for show. Cut back where it is wise, so that what remains has room to matter.
Mountain above Lake: the lake gives up its water to green the slopes above it. Hold your temper and rein in passing urges, so that what you give up feeds something higher.
When your own work is done, go quickly to help others. Still, weigh how much you can give without draining them or yourself.
Hold steady; this isn't the moment to set off on a venture. You can help others best here without giving yourself away.
When three travel together, one tends to fall away; when one travels alone, a companion appears. Close bonds come in twos.
As you trim away your own faults, others come gladly to your side. Changing yourself is what draws them.
Something good comes to you that nothing can stand against, not even ten pairs of oracle tortoises. Receive it gracefully.
You gain without taking anything from anyone. Others gather to help, and you come to belong to something larger than your own household.
growth, generosity, initiative, improvement

A time of increase: what comes from above flows down to strengthen what lies below. It is a good moment to begin something worthwhile, even to cross wide water. Use the momentum generously, for the good of others as well as your own.
Wind above Thunder: each strengthens the other, wind driving the thunder and thunder stirring the wind. When you see something good, take it up; when you find a fault in yourself, let it go.
This upswing gives you the strength to do something significant. Put it to work for a worthwhile purpose and the effort is well spent.
Something good comes to you that nothing can stand against. Stay steady and sincere, and offer what you receive back to something larger than yourself.
Growth reaches you through difficult events. Act truthfully, keep to the middle, and be open with those who need to know; then the hardship serves a purpose.
If you walk the middle road and speak plainly to those in charge, they are likely to listen. Someone trusted like this can help carry a big change, even a move to a new home.
If your kindness is real, there is no need to ask whether it will be noticed. Genuine goodwill tends to be recognized and returned.
Someone who adds to no one's good invites others to strike back. A changeable heart that only takes stands on poor footing.
resolve, truth, openness, decision

Pressure has built up and a breakthrough is due, like water about to burst its banks. Name the problem openly and honestly, in the right place, even if speaking up feels risky. Resolve matters, but it should come from clarity and fairness, not from force or a fight.
Lake above Heaven: water risen up to the sky, ready to pour down. Share what you have freely, and don't rest on the good you've already done.
All your strength has gone into your toes, itching to stride ahead. Rushing into something you aren't yet equal to is a mistake.
A cry of alarm rings out in the night, and you are already prepared. Ready and watchful, you have nothing to fear.
Wearing your determination on your face invites trouble. Hold your resolve inwardly, even if it means walking alone through the rain, splashed and misunderstood; that is not wrong.
Rubbed raw where you sit, you can neither stay put nor walk easily. Letting yourself be led like a sheep would ease the regret, though you may not believe this advice when you hear it.
Clearing weeds that keep growing back takes firm, steady resolve. Stay in the middle and you keep yourself clear.
No warning cry, no one calling out: the matter slips by unnoticed. What you leave unaddressed tends to return in the end.
encounter, temptation, influence, discernment

Something unexpected comes to meet you, a single influence slipping in beneath a great deal of strength. It may be bold and charming, but it isn't wise to hand it the keys or bind yourself to it. Welcome the meeting while keeping your own judgment in charge.
Wind below Heaven: the wind travels everywhere under the sky, touching all things. Make your intentions plainly known, the way a good leader sends word to every corner.
Put a firm brake on this early, as you would on a rolling cart. Even a scrawny pig can run riot if left alone; letting it run its course invites trouble.
There is a fish in your basket: the situation is in your keeping. Handle it gently yourself rather than passing it on to guests.
Rubbed raw where you sit, you find walking hard and you hesitate. Staying aware of the danger keeps you from serious harm.
The basket is empty of fish: you have lost touch with those you needed. Ignoring the people around you leaves you empty-handed.
A melon ripens out of sight beneath the shade of willow leaves. Keep your gifts quiet and let things mature; what is meant for you can drop into your hands in its own time.
You meet the world with lowered horns, proud and aloof. It may feel lonely and awkward, but your distance harms no one.
community, gathering, shared purpose, preparedness

People are coming together around something they share, like water collecting in a lake. A gathering needs a center: a person or purpose worth rallying to, and real offerings of time and effort. Take part fully, and prepare for the surprises any crowd can bring.
Lake above Earth: water pools where the land lies low. When many gather, keep your tools in order and your wits about you, so the unforeseen doesn't catch you off guard.
You mean well but don't follow through, so things swing between confusion and closeness. Call out for help; one firm handshake can turn worry into laughter.
Let yourself be drawn in; it is a good pull. When your heart is sincere, even a small offering is enough.
You gather with others amid sighs, feeling like an outsider. Joining anyway is right, even if it costs you a little pride.
Your effort to bring people together stands on good footing. Doing it for the group rather than for yourself keeps it clean.
You hold the central place in this gathering. If some aren't yet with you in heart, stay steadily true and their trust can grow.
Lament and tears, because your openness hasn't been returned. Sincere sorrow is no mistake, and it may move others to come closer.
growth, effort, steadiness, ascent

Like a young tree rising through the soil, progress now comes from patient, steady growth. Seek out people who can help and support you, and don't be anxious. Keep moving toward the light, one small step at a time.
Wind (wood) within Earth: a plant rising up out of the ground. Build something great by piling up many small, faithful acts.
Others welcome your rise and trust you. Going up with their confidence behind you is a very good start.
Sincerity counts for more than display. Even a modest offering, given honestly, is enough.
You push upward into an empty city, with no one standing in your way. Go ahead, without overthinking why it seems so easy.
You are given a place of honor, like a king's offering on a sacred mountain. Take it with humility and gratitude.
Climb steadily, step by step, like going up a staircase. Patience at each stage keeps the rise secure.
You are pushing upward in the dark, unable to see where you are going. Keep on only with steady, honest effort, not blind ambition.
exhaustion, constraint, integrity, inner strength

The lake has drained and you feel hemmed in and worn out. This is a time when words carry little weight, so let your conduct and your steadiness speak. Someone strong in spirit can bend under pressure without breaking, and come through still themselves.
Water beneath the Lake: the lake has emptied downward and lies dry. Even when your strength runs low, stay true to what you have set your heart on.
You sit stuck on a tree stump, then drift down into a dark valley. Dwelling on your low mood makes the darkness last longer, so start looking for a way out.
You feel weighed down from within, even with food and drink in front of you. Help may be closer than it looks; stay quiet and devoted rather than rushing out.
You lean against rock and grab at thorns, and when you come home, the one you hoped to find isn't there. Pushing against what can't be moved only wounds you.
You come very slowly, held back inside a golden carriage, comfortable but stuck. It is awkward, but you do get there in the end.
You are pressed from above and below, hampered by those in high office. Gladness comes slowly, and quiet devotion helps more than force.
Tangled in creeping vines, you tell yourself any move will be a mistake. Once you face your regret and decide to act, you can break free.
source, community, renewal, depth

Towns change and people come and go, but the well stays where it is, never running dry and never overflowing. It is a deep, shared source that serves everyone who draws from it. Care for the rope and the jar: if you stop short of the water or crack the vessel, the source can't reach you.
Water above Wind (wood): a wooden bucket lifts water up from below. Encourage others in their work and help them support one another.
No one drinks from a muddy well, and even animals pass by an old, neglected one. Let what has gone stagnant in you be cleared out.
Small fish dart in the shallows of the well, and the jar is cracked and leaking. Your gifts are being spent on trivial things.
The well has been cleaned, but no one draws from it, and that is a quiet sorrow. Good water is waiting, and a clear-sighted leader would put it to use for all.
The well is being lined with stone. Pausing to repair and strengthen yourself is time well spent.
The well water runs clear and cold from its spring, fresh enough to drink. Something good and refreshing is within reach; let it be drawn up and shared.
The water is drawn up freely and the well is left uncovered. A source that is open and reliable serves everyone well.
change, renewal, timing, trust

Something has outgrown its old shape, and a real change is coming due. It only takes hold when the moment is ripe and people can see why it is needed. Prepare it carefully, explain it honestly, and when the day comes, act. Regret fades once the change proves itself.
Fire below and Lake above: water and flame push against each other until one transforms the other. Watch how the seasons turn and keep track of your own timing, so you know when a change belongs.
Hold steady for now, wrapped in patience like tough hide. The change you sense is real, but its hour has not arrived.
The ground is prepared and the time is right. Begin the change now; you have earned the trust it needs.
Rushing ahead would go badly, and so would endless hesitation. Talk it through, listen until the same answer comes back three times, then commit.
You act from conviction, not grievance, and others can feel it. Changing the way things are run now brings good results.
Change like a tiger: bold, clear and plain for everyone to see. People believe in it before any proof is needed.
The great change is done; now refine the details, as a leopard's coat settles into its pattern. Don't push for more upheaval, but let things settle and hold to what has been won.
transformation, nourishment, culture, refinement

The cauldron is the vessel where raw ingredients become a meal worth sharing. This is a time to cook things through: to turn talent, effort and what you have been given into something that feeds others. Treat your gifts with care and something lasting comes of it.
Wind below, as wood, feeding Fire above: the flame keeps the cauldron working. Stand steady in your proper place, keep your purpose clear, and let what is in you be slowly transformed.
Tip the cauldron over and empty out the old residue before you cook. Even an unlikely start can lead somewhere good once the vessel is clean.
There is real food in your cauldron. Others may envy it, but they cannot touch what you have truly made, so keep your attention on the work.
The handles have shifted and no one can lift the pot; your best work goes untasted for now. Be patient: like rain after a dry spell, recognition comes and the tension eases.
The cauldron's legs give way and the meal spills. Taking on more than you can carry, or leaning on the wrong helpers, makes a mess, so be honest about your limits.
The cauldron has yellow handles and golden carrying rings: you are approachable, steady and easy to work with. That openness draws capable people to you, so keep to it.
The cauldron has rings of jade, hard yet softly gleaming. Strength and gentleness are in balance, good counsel flows freely, and the way ahead is open.
shock, awakening, composure, reflection

A thunderclap: sudden news or an upheaval that shakes everyone around you. Fear comes first, then relief and even laughter once the shock has passed. The one who keeps hold of what matters through the noise comes out stronger. Let the jolt wake you rather than unseat you.
Thunder on Thunder, one roll after another. When the ground shakes, set your life in order and look honestly at yourself, so the next shock finds you steady.
The shock arrives and your heart jumps, then you laugh with relief. Being shaken awake early is a blessing.
The shock brings danger and you may lose things you valued. Get to higher ground and don't chase after what is gone; in time what truly matters finds its way back, or stops mattering.
The shock leaves you dazed. Let it move you to act, and you will come through it.
The shock gets stuck in the mud, and you can neither push back nor move forward. Wait for firmer ground before trying again.
Shocks keep coming, back and forth. Stay centered: nothing essential is lost, and there is still work you can do.
Panic spreads and everyone stares around wildly, so pushing ahead now would go badly. Step back before the turmoil reaches you, even if others talk about your caution.
stillness, rest, boundaries, meditation

Like a mountain, be still. This is a time to quiet both body and mind, to stop moving when moving would not help. Rest in the moment without reaching past it, and the restless pull of other people's demands loosens its grip. Knowing when to stop is its own kind of wisdom.
Mountain beside Mountain, solid and unmoving. Keep your thoughts within the situation you are actually in, and let them rest there.
Keep your toes still: stop before you even start. Pausing at the very beginning costs nothing and keeps you steady.
Your legs are held still, but you are being carried along by someone else's momentum and cannot stop it. You may feel uneasy; notice that, and don't pretend otherwise.
Stillness forced on your middle becomes rigidity, and holding everything down by sheer will leaves the heart feeling choked. Ease up and breathe.
You quiet your whole torso, your sense of self. It is not complete calm yet, but it is real progress.
Keep your jaw still and choose your words with care. Speaking less, and in good order, leaves nothing to regret.
Stillness has become part of who you are, calm and generous. This settled heart brings good fortune.
gradual progress, patience, steadiness, growth

Development comes step by step, the way a tree grows on a mountainside. Lasting progress cannot be hurried; it follows its proper order, as a good partnership is built slowly and honestly. Keep a steady pace and things fall into place.
Mountain below and Wind above, like a tree on a mountain that grows slowly and becomes a landmark. Let your character grow the same way, and quietly lift those around you.
The wild goose edges toward the shore. You are new and alone and people may criticize, but going slowly and learning as you go is fine.
The wild goose reaches a broad rock. You have found secure footing, so eat, rest and share your good fortune with others.
The wild goose wanders onto the dry plateau, too far from water, and pressing on alone leads nowhere good. Stay where you belong and protect what you have built.
The wild goose lands in a tree, which is not its natural place. Look for a flat branch: adapt and be flexible, and you will find somewhere safe to rest.
The wild goose reaches the summit. For a while you may feel isolated or misunderstood, even by those close to you, but trust that in time the distance can close.
The wild goose rises to the clouds. Your journey is complete, and the way you lived it becomes an example others can follow.
commitment, position, tact, patience

You are entering an arrangement where you do not set the terms, as a young bride once entered a household not her own. Charging ahead or demanding more than your place allows will backfire. Act with tact, keep your expectations honest, and remember that every bond only lasts if it is built on more than impulse.

Lake below and Thunder above: thunder stirs the lake, and the water moves where the excitement leads. Keep the long run in mind from the very first step, and you will recognize a passing stir for what it is.
You come in at a lower rank than you hoped. Like someone limping who still walks, you can make real progress through quiet, loyal effort.
Like someone with one eye who still sees, you are let down by someone you counted on. Stay true to your own inner vision.
Eager for a place, you are tempted to accept a lesser one that doesn't fit you. Better to wait than to lower yourself.
You hold out past the expected time. That is fine: a bond worth having is often worth waiting for.
Your quiet dignity matters more than outward display, like a bride dressed more plainly than her attendants. Like the moon just short of full, this modesty brings good fortune.
The basket is empty and the ritual is hollow, all form and no substance. Going through the motions brings nothing, so look for what is real.
abundance, fullness, peak, clarity

This is a time of fullness: energy, light and opportunity at their peak. Don't spoil it by worrying that it will pass. Be like the sun at noon, shining on everything without holding back. Every peak gives way in time, so make good use of this one.
Fire below and Thunder above: lightning and thunder arrive together, clarity joined with force. It is a moment to settle open questions and weigh things fairly and decisively.
You meet someone whose strengths complement your own. Work together for a full cycle; that is no mistake, and it will be noticed.
A curtain so heavy you can see stars at midday: intrigue or confusion clouds the situation. Pushing only breeds distrust, so hold to your sincerity and let it open the way.
Shadows thicken until even faint stars show at noon, and your hands are tied. This is not your fault; wait for the light to return.
The curtain is still heavy, but you meet an ally of a like mind. Together you find your way back into the light.
You welcome capable people and listen to their advice. Their help brings blessing and recognition.
A grand house is walled off from everyone, and looking out you see no one, because you shut them all out. Fullness turned into pride ends in loneliness.
travel, transition, modesty, caution

You are the traveler, passing through places that are not your home. Small, steady steps succeed here. Be courteous, keep your needs simple and hold to your own principles. A stranger who stays modest and careful finds welcome wherever the road leads.
Mountain below and Fire above: a fire races over the mountain and does not stay. Think things through, weigh them with care, and settle disagreements quickly instead of letting them linger.
Fussing over petty things on the road wins you no respect. Keep your dignity and don't get lost in small grievances.
You arrive at an inn with your belongings and find a loyal helper. Inner calm keeps you safe and well supported.
Through arrogance or meddling, the inn burns down and your helper walks away. Mind your conduct far from home.
You have shelter and the means to defend yourself, but your heart is not at ease. A place to stay is not the same as being home.
With one well-aimed arrow you bring down the pheasant. A fitting gift or skill opens doors and earns you a place.
The bird's nest burns: you laugh at first, then you grieve. Careless pride costs you your gentleness and your home.
gentleness, persistence, influence, penetration

Like wind that keeps blowing until it reaches every corner, gentle and steady influence achieves what force cannot. Small, consistent efforts carry you far. Have a clear direction, and seek out people who can see further than you.
Wind following Wind, one breeze after another. Explain your purpose clearly and repeat it gently, then follow through.
Forward, then back, then forward again: indecision wears you down. Borrow a soldier's discipline and choose a direction.
Something hidden is at work beneath the surface. Bring it into the light, with help if you need it, and the trouble clears.
You weigh it and weigh it again until the chance has passed. Too much deliberation becomes its own embarrassment.
Regret falls away. Modesty joined with energy brings in a rich harvest, much like a successful hunt.
The start was rough, but it can still end well. Think it through before the change and review it afterwards.
You have probed too deep and spent your strength and your means. Pressing further would only hurt, so stop and recover.
joy, openness, conversation, friendship

Joy is shared here, open and easy, like friends talking over a meal. True gladness comes from inner steadiness, not from flattery or chasing pleasure. Be warm and sincere, and others gladly join in. Joy that is honest lasts.
Two lakes joined side by side, each keeping the other fresh. Gather with friends to talk, learn and practice together, so that good company refreshes everyone.
Quiet, self-contained contentment. You need nothing outside yourself to feel glad, and that brings good fortune.
Joy rooted in sincerity keeps you steady and away from tempting distractions. Regret has nothing to hold on to.
Pleasures come looking for you, offering easy delight. Chasing them leaves you emptier than before.
You weigh one pleasure against another and cannot rest. Choose the higher one, let go of the lower, and real joy follows.
You are trusting something that quietly wears you down. Be careful where you place your confidence.
You are being drawn along by what charms and flatters you. Notice who or what is leading you, and whether you want to follow.
dissolving, release, reunion, flow

Like wind breaking up ice on water, this is a time to dissolve what has hardened: grudges, rigid habits, walls between people. When the ego softens, people can come together again around something larger than themselves. A shared purpose, or something you hold sacred, helps the reuniting happen. It is a good time for a bold undertaking.
Wind blowing over Water, scattering what has frozen. Turn toward what you hold sacred and build something in common that brings scattered people back together.
Deal with the misunderstanding early, with strength and speed, before it grows. Quick help now brings good fortune.
As things come apart, hurry to what steadies you. Return to your foundations and regret melts away.
Set your own concerns aside for something larger. Letting go of self-interest leaves nothing to regret.
Step away from your faction or clique for the sake of a wider good. What looks like scattering gathers into something greater, though few see it at first.
One clear, unifying idea breaks the tension the way sweat breaks a fever. Holding to the center now is right.
Remove yourself, and those close to you, from harm's way. Keeping your distance now is the wise choice.
boundaries, moderation, measure, discipline

Healthy limits give life its shape, the way the joints of bamboo give it strength. Know what is enough. But limits that are too harsh cannot last, and they turn bitter if forced, on yourself or anyone else. Find the measure that leaves room to breathe.
Lake below and Water above: the lake holds only so much before it overflows. Decide what your measures are, and examine what good conduct means to you.
Stay inside your own door for now. Knowing when not to act, and keeping your own counsel, is wise.
The time to step out has come, yet you stay behind your gate. Holding back now is a missed chance.
Without any limit you end up with regret. Own it honestly, and you can begin again.
Limits you accept without strain, easy and natural, bring success.
You set limits on yourself first, and you set them gently. People follow willingly, and this earns respect.
Harsh, bitter limits cannot be kept up for long. Sometimes they are necessary for a while, but loosen them when you can.
sincerity, trust, openness, inner truth

Inner truth is a heart open enough to understand even those who are hardest to reach. When you are sincere, people and situations respond, much as the wind moves the surface of a lake. This kind of trust can carry you through great undertakings. Stay honest, and it holds.
Wind blowing over the Lake, stirring its depths. Listen deeply and try to understand others before you pass judgment, leaning toward mercy.
Be ready, and rely on your own inner steadiness. Secret schemes or hidden dependencies only unsettle you.
A crane calls from the shade and its young answer. Sincerity carries a long way; offer what you have and share it with those whose hearts answer yours.
You tie your mood to someone else: now drumming, now silent, now crying, now singing. Your happiness rests outside yourself.
Like the moon nearly full, you turn toward a higher source and let a companion go their own way. That parting is no mistake.
Your sincerity binds people together like a strong cord. Leading through trust is right.
A rooster's crow tries to reach the sky: words outrunning what is really there. Persisting in empty bravado goes badly.
caution, humility, detail, restraint

This is a time for small things, not great ones. Like a bird that should stay low rather than climb into the storm, keep your aims modest and attend carefully to details. Excess in small, humble ways, such as a little more care or a little more courtesy, is fine. Overreaching is not.
Mountain below and Thunder above: thunder on the mountain sounds near, not far. Lean toward a little extra respect in what you do, sincere grief in loss, and thrift in what you spend.
The bird tries to fly before it is ready and comes to grief. Stay in the nest a while longer.
You don't reach the person you hoped for, but you meet someone close to them. Accepting the more modest connection is wise.
You feel too confident to be careful, but someone may come from behind. Guard against what you are overlooking.
Meet things as they come rather than pushing ahead. Going forward now is risky, so hold your position and stay alert.
Dense clouds, but no rain yet. You can't do it alone; seek out capable people who are keeping a low profile.
You overshoot the mark, like a bird flying far past where it should land. Going too far brings trouble of its own making.
completion, vigilance, maintenance, balance

Things are in order, with everything in its place, like a crossing just completed. That balance is fragile. Things start out well, but disorder creeps in when people relax. Tend to small details now and stay watchful, so the success you have lasts.
Water above Fire: the kettle boils, but it could spill over and put out the flame. Think ahead about what might go wrong and prepare for it before it happens.
You brake as the wheels start to roll and only your tail gets wet. Holding back at the start of a surge keeps you safe.
You lose something that marks your place, and you feel unseen. Don't run after it; what is truly yours tends to come back in its own time.
A long, hard campaign succeeds only after years of effort. Choose carefully whom you rely on along the way.
Even good cloth begins to fray. Watch for small leaks and flaws, and stay careful all day long.
A lavish offering means less than a small, sincere one. What counts is the heart behind the act.
Having crossed, you look back and get your head wet. Don't linger in the danger you have just passed through; keep moving forward.
transition, almost there, care, promise

You are close to the end of a crossing, but not there yet. Success is possible, as long as you don't let your guard down at the last moment, like the young fox that gets its tail wet just short of the far bank. Careful attention through to the finish turns promise into completion.
Fire above Water: each moves away from the other and they have not yet met. Tell things apart with care, and put each one where it belongs before you try to bring them together.
Charging ahead too early, you get your tail wet. Wait until you can see the whole crossing.
Brake the wheels: ready, but not yet moving. Steady patience brings good fortune.
You cannot force the last stretch with what you have. Change your approach, find new means or helpers, and then make the leap.
Steady effort pays off and regret fades. A long, hard push is finally rewarded.
Steady and sincere, you let your inner light shine, and others see it is genuine. Good fortune.
Celebrate with trust and good cheer. But don't lose your head in the celebration and forget what got you here.
